transcript:
Meeting Date: 2026-12-02
Start Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Liam O'Shea (Rivergate - CISO), Marisol Vega (Rivergate - Head of Cloud Ops), Daniel Park (Rivergate - Director of Risk)

[00:00] Jordan: All right thanks everyone for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intros — I'm Jordan, AE on the account, and Priya is our lead SE on infra and incident response.
[00:12] Priya: hi all, thanks. quick note I'm in PST so apologies if I jump around a little.
[00:18] Liam: Hey Jordan, Priya, thanks. We wanted to walk through incident response and B C D R — RTO RPO and escalation details — before we move forward with a pilot.
[00:30] Jordan: sounds good. At a high level we typically offer a 99.9x SLA for hosted endpoints, and Dedicated customers can get 99.95 or 99.99 depending on contract. For banks we usually look at Dedicated with private control plane, VPC, and HSM integration.
[00:50] Marisol: can you clarify the RTO and RPO assumptions for Dedicated? Our internal bar for critical customer-facing sys is RTO <= 1 hour and RPO <= 15 minutes, but for some payments pipelines we want closer to near-zero RPO.
[01:05] Priya: yeah. Our standard BCDR offering for Dedicated is configurable — we typically target RTO 30-60m for full failover to a hot standby region, RPO depends on whether you enable continuous KV cache replication and write-ahead logs; we can get to sub-15m RPO with streaming replication and sync commits; near-zero is possible but requires stricter persistence and synchronous replication which increases latency/cost.
[01:35] Daniel: when you say "KV cache replication" is that the same as your prefix/KV cache in the inference runtime? we need to understand what state is persisted vs ephemeral.
[01:45] Priya: good point — the runtime maintains a KV cache for in-flight sessions; that's ephemeral for latency. For persistent state we rely on model artifacts and request logs. For low RPO on customer data (requests/inputs) we recommend enabling request journaling into an encrypted log store and cross-region replication — that gives you recoverable inputs within the RPO window.
[02:10] Liam: any limitations on log retention and encryption? regulatory requires logs for 7 years for certain transactions.
[02:18] Jordan: we support configurable audit log retention; default is 90 days for hosted but Dedicated customers can set retention and export logs to your S3-like endpoints or to your SIEM. Encryption at rest is AES-256, we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key custody; we also support Bring Your Own Key.
[02:40] Marisol: ok on KMS — do you support AWS KMS and external HSMs? we operate multi-cloud and have centralized key management.
[02:48] Priya: yes AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault are supported; for Private we can integrate with on-prem HSMs over PKCS#11 or KMIP. There may be an initial onboarding checklist for key rotation and access controls.
[03:03] Daniel: escalation — who gets paged first in a Sev1? what's the runbook outline?
[03:10] Jordan: typical escalation is: Redwood on-call (level 1) -> SE on-call (level 2) -> Engineering owner -> Exec engagement if not resolved per SLA. For Dedicated customers we map a named support engineer and can include customer contacts in the on-call rotation for joint incident calls.
[03:30] Priya: we also do periodic runbook reviews with enterprise customers. We'll create a joint runbook that lists on-call contacts, secondary contacts, playbooks for failover, verification steps, rollback, and postmortem expectations including timelines for RCA.
[03:45] Marisol: do you provide a runbook template we can adapt?
[03:48] Jordan: yes we'll share templates and a sample playbook from a similar financial customer, redacted of course.
[03:55] Liam: what's your SLA credit policy for downtime? what does 99.95 mean in monthly downtime minutes?
[04:03] Jordan: 99.95% is about ~21.6 minutes/month; 99.99% is ~4.3 minutes/month. Credits depend on severity and contract — we'll share the exact SLA language in the security pack.
[04:18] Daniel: how do you measure availability — at the API layer, per region, per model?
[04:25] Priya: we measure at the endpoint/route level and per region; we also can instrument per-model telemetry. For Dedicated we can provide token-level latency and success rate dashboards in the Console.
[04:40] Marisol: can you walk through an example escalation timeline — say an incident hits at 02:00 UTC and causes degraded inference in primary region?
[04:50] Priya: sure. T0: detection via synthetic probes and customer alerting; T+5m: auto-routing to warm standby or fallback model (if configured); T+15m: SE triage and if needed open joint bridge; T+30-60m: failover to hot-standby region if not contained; T+1-4h: full mitigation and remediation; RCA within 3-5 business days and postmortem within 10 business days typically.
[05:20] Liam: three questions — 1) can we control auto-fallback to cheaper models? 2) do fallback events count against our SLA? 3) what's the communication cadence during an incident?
[05:33] Jordan: 1) yes policy-based routing allows fallback to model variants or lower-cost tiers; 2) fallback itself is part of graceful degradation strategy — SLA triggers are based on customer-facing success rate; specifics in contract; 3) we provide incident updates every 15-30 minutes on Sev1s plus a dedicated bridge and postmortem.
[05:55] Daniel: audit logs — is everything PII redacted automatically or do we need to scrub at the client side?
[06:03] Priya: we don't automatically redact PII from request payloads — we recommend tokenization or client-side redaction for sensitive fields. We do support field-level encryption and can advice on redaction best-practices.
[06:20] Marisol: about RBAC and SSO — we want SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning and role based access for ops vs developers.
[06:29] Jordan: we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC that maps to roles: admin, operator, auditor, developer. For Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your IdP and lock down console and API access.
[06:48] Liam: curious about audit trail integrity — do you timestamp and sign logs? chain of custody?
[06:55] Priya: logs are timestamped and stored with integrity controls; Dedicated customers can enable append-only storage and ship to their own immutable storage for chain-of-custody needs.
[07:10] Jordan: returning to RTO/RPO — Marisol said their target is RTO <= 1h, RPO <= 15m. Priya do we have any blockers to that for Rivergate?
[07:20] Priya: technically achievable. Key items: enable request journaling, cross-region replication enabled with sync or near-sync, and agreement on failover playbook. Also for near-zero RPO you'd want synchronous writes to durable store which will impact latency and cost — we can scope performance tradeoffs in the pilot.
[07:40] Marisol: cost is a concern — synchronous replication will raise per-token cost, can you quantify?
[07:48] Priya: we'll run benchmarks in the pilot; rough order of magnitude is 10-25% added latency for sync writes and corresponding infra costs. We'll provide explicit cost scenarios in the benchmarking spreadsheet.
[08:05] Liam: regarding incident response contacts — we'd like primary contacts in Redwood to be available via pager and have escalation to an on-call SE within 15 minutes.
[08:15] Jordan: we can commit to on-call SE triage within 15 minutes for Dedicated customers under the enterprise SLA. We'll document exact paging channels and SSO/2FA for access to the bridge.
[08:30] Marisol: can we require that certain changes (model upgrades, infra patches) go through a change review with us? We need change windows.
[08:39] Priya: yes change control is part of the Dedicated plan; we can agree maintenance windows and pre-notices; emergency changes follow the incident runbook.
[08:50] Daniel: do you offer a sandbox for failover testing that mirrors production?
[08:55] Jordan: yes we can provision a pilot cluster that mirrors your production topology and run the failover drill; Priya will handle the technical setup.
[09:03] Priya: action: I'll send a test plan template and schedule options. We'll need Rivergate's network ACLs and support for peering; also service accounts for cross-region replication.
[09:18] Marisol: timeline wise, we want pilot in January with production cutover H1 2027 if everything passes.
[09:25] Jordan: good — we'll align resources. any regulatory items we missed — PCI/regulatory retention specifics?
[09:33] Liam: PCI applies to some payments flows, we may need segmented processing and tokenization. We'll share specifics in the runbook.
[09:40] Priya: understood. We'll include tokenization recommendations and show where we recommend client-side processing.
[09:48] Daniel: on SLA credits and legal — we'll have legal review standard SLA; can you send contract language for review?
[09:55] Jordan: yes, Jordan to send draft SLA and contract excerpt along with SOC2 and BCP docs.
[10:02] Marisol: quick nit — sometimes Fireflies outputs have transcription noise; please double-check the security pack attachments.
[10:10] Jordan: will do. ok let's recap next steps.

Recap (approx timestamps):
- Jordan to send SOC2 report, SLA language, security pack (00:55)
- Priya to send failover test plan and schedule pilot cluster (09:03)
- Rivergate (Marisol) to share runbook and contact matrix (09:18)
- Follow up technical deep dive 2026-12-16 14:00 ET (agreed) (00:00)

Close: thanks all, meeting ended 15:48 UTC
